ground_truth.description: The suppression check relies on semantic/vector search (`search(query="stage1_flag_suppression", ...)`) to locate a specific task's suppression record. Vector search returns only a bounded top-k ranked by similarity, so when suppression records exist for many tasks (or the corpus is large), the record for the target task_id may not appear in the results at all. The check then concludes 'no suppression in effect' and emits the flag — a false negative that exactly matches the flagged symptom (review passed but escalation_created). A deterministic metadata lookup (e.g. get_memories_by_metadata / count_memories_by_metadata filtered on kind+task_id) is required.

The search query string is the generic literal "stage1_flag_suppression" and does not include the target task_id, so records for all other tasks compete for the limited top-k slots and can crowd out the relevant task's record, again causing the target's suppression to be missed.

The validity test requires `metadata.task_id == <N>` as an integer, but metadata persisted through Mem0 may store the task_id as a string; a strict integer equality check would then reject a genuine suppression record and fall through to emitting the flag (false negative). The comparison should be type-normalized.

The new 'Flag Suppression Check' prompt section tells the Stage 1 LLM not to 'write a stage1_flag_marker' for a suppressed task, but the LLM never writes those markers: flag_dedup.dedup_flags writes one in code for every signatured entry of report.items_flagged, called from MemoryConsolidatorStage.run after the LLM finishes. The section never tells the model to omit the task from items_flagged or from its flag_for_stage2 Mem0 relay (which the 'Stage 2 Flag Relay' section requires to be mirrored into flagged_items), and the next section tells it to 'emit findings naturally'. A model that follows the text literally still flags task 452, dedup_flags still writes the marker, and the write/detect/delete contamination cycle the task targets continues; there is no code-level suppression check at the point the marker is written.

The section declares a 'canonical' suppression-record schema (metadata.kind='stage1_flag_suppression', metadata.task_id=<N>, fixed content string) and tells the model that any record failing either metadata field means 'no suppression; proceed normally', but nothing in the repo writes records in that shape (no writer, constant or documented procedure), and the change does not establish that the two suppression records the task cites for task 452 (mem0:87643d99, mem0:ff84b3fb) carry those metadata keys. If they do not, the strict predicate rejects them and the check is a no-op for the very task it was written for. Whether those live records conform cannot be confirmed from the repository.

The task requires skipping flag emission only 'if a suppression record exists and the task remains in the suppressed status'. The added rule drops the status condition: any matching suppression record suppresses all flags for that task unconditionally and indefinitely, so if task 452 leaves 'deferred' its legitimate flags are silently swallowed for as long as the record exists.

The closing paragraph of the new section is reviewer-facing rationale (the 'contamination cycle motivating this check' narrative and the claim that suppression is 'authoritative over' a post-processing dedup the model has no ordering relationship with). It ships in the system prompt on every Stage 1 run and will drift; it also leaves unstated whether suppression applies in Remediation Mode, and it uses 'suppression' for a different concept than the flag_dedup.py module docstring, which says suppression lives in Stage 2's prompt.

No test covers the suppression behaviour. Because the change is prompt prose only, there is no executable path to test behaviourally (and the repo recently removed wording-pin meta-tests); behavioural coverage that a suppressed task_id yields no items_flagged entry and no stage1_flag_marker write becomes possible only once suppression is enforced in code. The task's test_strategy was empty.

The suppression record schema discriminates on metadata.kind, while the sibling Stage 1 control records (stage1_flag_marker) and the find_prior_memories filter convention use metadata.source, so readers of this family of Mem0 control records must know two discriminator keys, and the schema has no shared constant.

The new section calls the tool by its bare name search(...), whereas commit 645d08c82d (task 1174) deliberately converted this prompt's tool references to the fully qualified mcp__fused-memory__search listed in Available Tools.

The rule is phrased per candidate flag ('before writing any ...'), inviting one search tool call per flagged task per cycle, although the query string is the same for every task so a single search per run would suffice. Minor cost concern only.

task.title: Stage 1 system prompt: add pre-emission suppression check before writing any stage1_flag_marker for task 452
task.description: Stage 1 (memory_consolidator) must search for active suppression records BEFORE emitting any stage1_flag_marker for task 452. Without this check, Stage 1 may write violating markers even when suppression is active, requiring repeated remediation runs to delete them. Four violations have occurred across cycles 38, 39, 51, and potentially future cycles.
task.details:
Root cause: Stage 1 flag-dedup logic writes new markers for tasks without first checking if a suppression record exists that prohibits emission. For task 452 (autopilot_video: 'Investigate 2026-04-21 mass task reset', status=deferred since 2026-04-27), two authoritative suppression memories exist: mem0:87643d99 and mem0:ff84b3fb (autopilot_video project). 

Fix required: At the start of the flag-emission loop in Stage 1 system prompt, add a step: "Before writing any stage1_flag_marker, search for active suppression records for the target task_id. If a suppression record exists and the task remains in the suppressed status, skip flag emission." This prevents the contamination cycle where Stage 1 writes a violating flag → Stage 3 detects it → remediation run deletes it → next cycle Stage 1 writes it again.

Suppression enforcement memories (autopilot_video project):
- 87643d99-57b1-40e7-a62c-3b36481bb2cb: STAGE 1 FLAG SUPPRESSION directive for task 452
- ff84b3fb-715e-4e65-a444-94b3bd2050fa: STAGE 1 FLAG SUPPRESSION UPDATE (cycle-51 violation cleanup)

The fix applies to the Stage 1 system prompt in the dark-factory reconciliation harness, specifically the pre-emission check step.
